svg.text: Hardware performance counters: the cycle equation, counted by the chip itself
cycles = N + 5 + L + 3F + R + K + I + D (docs/MATH.md). Each term has a read-only counter in src/Control_Status_Register_File.sv, readable with csrr.
Program 19 at the moment it reads the counters: rdcycle says 192; the counters add up to 96 + 5 + 12 + 3 x 7 + 2 + 24 + 12 + 23 = 195.
The 3-cycle difference: some counted bubbles and instructions have not reached WRITEBACK yet when rdcycle is read in EXECUTE. At the end of a program the two sides are exactly equal (make math).
How to use them: read a counter before and after a piece of code (csrr t0, hpmcounter4 ... csrr t1, hpmcounter4); the difference is how many
times that event happened in between. programs/19_performance_counters.s adds them all up and checks the sum against rdcycle.
Real CPUs have hundreds of such events (Intel's "top-down" method builds exactly this kind of CPI stack from them); the counters are 64 bits,
split into halves with a registered carry so they never slow down the clock.
